exposure: Double-embryo transfer (DET) leading to singleton birth
Single-embryo transfer (SET) leading to singleton birth
cohort: The study cohort included 1,115,863 singleton births, specifically 30,713 singletons born after SET and 5,123 after DET in Sweden between 2007 and 2017, with naturally conceived singletons serving as a reference group.
finding: The study found that double-embryo transfer (DET) leading to singleton birth was associated with a higher risk of adverse outcomes, including neonatal death, low birth weight, and very preterm birth, compared to single-embryo transfer (SET).
